note: 30 fixed synthetic tasks written for this suite (rule 4); each has one canonical target. A check is read by crates/mzdraw/tests/suite/check.rs: pieces are the canonical SMILES (mzlab-mol Mol::can) of the connected pieces of the final drawing, left to right when order is true; objects are the arrows, plus signs and texts, with their text and their place between pieces; edit_zone lists the ids a surgical edit may change, everything else of the start document must keep its id, element and position; std none means no std/1 finding.

tasks.words: Draw 4-chlorophenol.
Draw ethyl acetate.
Draw aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) as the neutral acid.
Draw paracetamol, N-(4-hydroxyphenyl)acetamide.
Draw cyclohexanone.
Draw nitrobenzene with the nitro group written in its charge-separated form: N+ carrying one N=O double bond and one single bond to an O-.
Draw L-alanine, (S)-2-aminopropanoic acid, neutral (not a zwitterion), with its stereocentre defined.
Draw pyridine.
Draw N-methylpyrrolidine, a five-membered saturated ring with one nitrogen that carries a methyl group.
Draw chloroform-d, CDCl3: one carbon with three chlorines and one deuterium, the deuterium drawn as an explicit atom of hydrogen with mass number 2.
Put a fluorine on the carbon para to the chlorine-bearing carbon. Touch nothing else.
Change the oxygen into sulfur. Touch nothing else.
Turn the methyl group into a hydroxymethyl group (add one oxygen to the methyl carbon). Touch nothing else.
Make the acid a carboxylate: give the single-bonded oxygen a charge of -1. Touch nothing else.
Remove the hydroxyl group (the oxygen and its bond). Touch nothing else.
Replace the carbonyl oxygen (the one with the double bond) by sulfur. Touch nothing else.
Extend the methyl group on the ester oxygen to an ethyl group (add one carbon). Touch nothing else.
Delete the ethylamine, the piece that contains the nitrogen, and keep ethanol. Touch nothing else.
Replace the hydroxyl group by an amino group (change the oxygen into nitrogen). Touch nothing else.
Draw a reaction scheme from left to right: ethanol, a plus sign, acetic acid, a reaction arrow carrying the condition text H+, and ethyl acetate.
Draw three separate structures in one row, left to right: toluene, pyridine, cyclohexanone. No arrows, no plus signs, no text.
Draw two salts side by side as separate ions, no plus signs and no arrows: sodium chloride on the left (Na+ then Cl-), potassium acetate on the right (acetate then K+).
Draw ethene and bromine (Br2, drawn as a Br-Br bond) left of a reaction arrow with the condition text CH2Cl2, with a plus sign between the two reactants, and 1,2-dibromoethane right of the arrow.

Draw the nitration of benzene: benzene, a plus sign, nitric acid (N+ with one N=O, one N-O- and one N-OH, written in the charge-separated form), a reaction arrow with the condition text H2SO4, nitrobenzene (charge-separated nitro group), a plus sign and water.
Draw ammonia, a plus sign, hydrogen chloride (H-Cl), a reaction arrow without text, and ammonium chloride as two separate ions (NH4+ then Cl-) with nothing between the ions.
Draw acetone and, to the right of it, a text note reading: solvent THF. Nothing else.
Draw ethene, a reaction arrow without text, and bromoethane.
Draw three structures in one row, left to right, no signs and no text: glycine, then alanine, then serine, all neutral and with no stereochemistry drawn (flat bonds only).
Draw a reaction scheme from left to right: methanol, a plus sign, benzoic acid, a reaction arrow with the condition text H2SO4, heat, methyl benzoate, a plus sign, water.
On the product (the structure right of the arrow), put a fluorine on the carbon para to the chlorine-bearing carbon. Touch nothing else: the reactant and the arrow stay exactly as they are.
